Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-08 11:00 AM PT
Duration: 54 minutes (recording started)
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood CSM), Mike Chen (Northbay CTO), Sara Lopez (Eng Mgr), Lily Tran (Product), Devon Brooks (Security), Anika Rao (Platform), Tommy (Network)

Summary: Quick activation + connectivity sprint to get pilot running. Covering VPC peering, SSO, RBAC, staging model pin, perf targets and go/no-go criteria for two-week pilot.
Topics: connectivity window, security packet, pilot scope, perf expectations, runbooks and rollback plan, monitoring hooks
Action items quick list (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Meyers: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, will do a quick rollcall, I'm Jordan AE on the account, priya is our se, carlos is csm - anybody new on the call?
[00:18] Mike Chen: mike here, devon's on sec but he might chime in, sara and lily from eng and product.
[00:24] Priya Anand: quick agenda, 1) connectivity and network pre-reqs 2) security docs and SSO 3) perf baseline and pilot scope 4) next steps and runbook handoff. sound good?
[00:34] Sara Lopez: yep that's good, we mostly want to make sure we can hit 100ms p95 on single-query flows in staging, and then tolerate spikes to like 300ms during bursts.
[00:46] Priya Anand: ok noted, staging SLA vs prod SLA we'll call out. one clarification on the network - are you planning VPC peering or private link?
[00:55] Tom(typo says Tommy): we're leaning to VPC peering, but we need to confirm CIDR ranges.
[01:02] Devon Brooks: security here - we need SOC two and iso documents, also audit log retention limits, and clarity on who can access logs. we typically require KMS integration.
[01:14] Jordan Meyers: yes we'll share the security packet, our SOC2 report and our iso summary, plus a checklist for KMS/HSM integration. note: some of the private deploy options require an extra eng kick-off.
[01:27] Priya Anand: let's talk perf briefly, we usually recommend warming the KV cash - excuse me KV cache - before the pilot to avoid cold start jitter. for your workloads (product search + summarization) we saw better p95 when prefix caching is enabled.
[01:43] Sara Lopez: KV cash, huh, ok. how do you guys recommend priming that, is that automatic?
[01:49] Priya Anand: we can run an automatic warmup when we deploy the model, it's part of the runtime config, or you can hit an endpoint with the sample prompt set. we'll coordinate the script.
[01:58] Lily Tran: what's the recommended model pinning? we want consistency during the pilot so results don't flip on us.
[02:05] Avery Lin: pin to the 1.4.3 variant that we validated in the perf run; we'll supply the model manifest and the exact hash. also we have a fallback variant for cost/capacity.
[02:18] Mike Chen: pricing question - if we use quantized variants during the pilot, does billing change?
[02:24] Jordan Meyers: billing is per-token regardless, but quantization reduces GPU footprint which reduces your committed spend under Dedicated. we'll send a simple cost comparison.
[02:36] Devon Brooks: about logs - where do they land? we need to ensure no PII gets stored, and if we have to redact we need docs.
[02:45] Carlos Vega: we have redaction hooks and you can set request-level retention. our Private deployments are customer-controlled for logs; hosted has configurable retention. we'll share the retention policy matrix.
[02:57] Sara Lopez: network window? how long does peering usually take?
[03:02] Anika Rao: our infra team prefers a maintenance window in which routing can be updated; depending on approvals usually 2-4 hours for a simple peering.
[03:11] Priya Anand: action wise, Devon we'll need the CIDR and proxy whitelist. we'll also need a service account for the peering handoff.
[03:20] Mike Chen: we'll try to get those by friday, 9/10.
[03:25] Jordan Meyers: great. Pilot scope — two-week pilot focused on user-facing search and a summarization endpoint. success criteria: p95 below 150ms in staging for single-turn search at 99th percentile of typical traffic, and no regression in quality vs baseline prompts.
[03:44] Lily Tran: for quality checks, can Redwood run evals against our prompt set and provide delta metrics?
[03:50] Priya Anand: yes we can run automated evals and also point to Redwood Optimize suggestions. we'll upload a report with rouge/semantic-similarity buckets.
[04:02] Sara Lopez: what about observability hooks? we want per-route token cost and latency breakdown.
[04:08] Avery Lin: Console exposes per-route charts, tracing and token-level costs, and you can export to your datadog or prometheus. we'll provide a sample dashboard json.
[04:19] Mike Chen: fallback behaviors — if the primary model is throttled do you have automatic fallback to a cheaper variant?
[04:26] Priya Anand: yes that is configurable in the rollout policy; we can set automatic fallback to a lower-cost quantized model after X% errors or latency breach. you can also have canary traffic by route.
[04:38] Devon Brooks: SSO - we use SAM-L via Okta, any gotchas?
[04:43] Jordan Meyers: we support SAML and OIDC, SSO setup is standard, we'll run a SSO test in staging. note sometimes attributes mapping needs manual mapping (roles->RBAC).
[04:55] Mike Chen: who will own runbook?
[04:58] Carlos Vega: Redwood CSM will own the initial runbook and we'll handoff a runbook template; call it co-owned during the pilot then customer ops takes over for prod.
[05:09] Sara Lopez: can we get a quick dry-run of the rollback? we want to ensure a rollback strategy if quality drops.
[05:15] Priya Anand: yes we'll include rollback steps in the runbook: pin older model hash, drain traffic, and re-route. we'll demo during the pilot kickoff.
[05:25] Jordan Meyers: timeline recap: send security packet today, get CIDR by 9/10, perf test by 9/15, pilot kickoff week of 9/20. any blockers?
[05:36] Mike Chen: procurement may want an enterprise addendum; do you have a starter template?
[05:40] Jordan Meyers: yes we'll send an initial template and the pricing sheet. procurement redlines are expected but that's fine.
[05:47] Lily Tran: small note on data residency - some logs need to stay in the eu region; we're mostly us-west but will flag if anything needs eu.
[05:58] Carlos Vega: we can scope data residency options in the security packet.
[06:04] Tommy (network): quick question: NAT behavior on the peering, will we need to open a specific port?
[06:09] Priya Anand: typically it's standard HTTPS egress, but we'll include the exact port list in the network checklist.
[06:17] Mike Chen: ok sounds good.
[06:20] Jordan Meyers: all right if no more questions we'll do a short demo of the Console quick-start for the staging run.
[06:27] [demo segment - screen share - short walkthrough of Console]
[06:40] Priya Anand: showing the model pin UI, rollout policies, and the per-route dashboards. note the trace view includes token split and KV cache hits, though sometimes the transcriptions show KV cash in the logs.
[06:58] Sara Lopez: seeing the traces helps. can the Console send alerts to our slack on p95 breaches?
[07:05] Avery Lin: yes, we have integration with slack and pagerduty. you can set thresholds on p95 and token count.
[07:13] Mike Chen: about the perf test - what environment will you run it in, dedicated or hosted?
[07:19] Priya Anand: we'll run it in a dedicated staging pool that mirrors your production-sized config; if you need a private deployment we can mirror that too but that adds setup time.
[07:30] Lily Tran: extra question — will you keep logs of prompts for evals? we need redaction, and also to ensure compliance.
[07:37] Carlos Vega: evals can be run on anonymized snapshots; we can also run locally if required.
[07:43] Devon Brooks: can Redwood's team access our pilot logs? we prefer limited access.
[07:48] Jordan Meyers: access can be limited; CSM will request access only for the pilot duration and all access will be logged.
[07:56] Mike Chen: good.
[08:00] Jordan Meyers: ok wrapping up, quick recap of next steps - I'll send the security packet and pricing; Priya runs perf; Devon gives CIDR; Sara shares prompts; we'll schedule the pilot kickoff.
[08:12] Sara Lopez: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[08:15] Lily Tran: thanks.
[08:17] Jordan Meyers: end of recording, bye.
